native_custom_check_ledger.native_title: Raffle state-changing entry points with external interactions are nonReentrant (except documented allowlist)
All quote-token safeTransfer calls are inside _transferQuote
Per-raffle configuration variables are written only by initialize()
status is written only by constructor/initialize/onERC721Received/requestDraw/enableRefunds/fulfillRandomWords
fulfillRandomWords: no explicit revert/require/assert, no external interaction, no loop
_settleWinningTicket performs no external interaction (storage-only settlement)
Prize transfers only in redeem/releaseSponsorPrize, each reads+writes prizeClaimed and verifies ownerOf
Raffle._update screens destinations via _isProtocolDestination and delegates to ERC721._update
No delegatecall/selfdestruct/ecrecover/blockhash/tx.origin/prevrandao in production contracts
createRaffle: clone -> initialize -> register(isRaffle) -> untrusted prize safeTransferFrom
unsettledPot written only by buyEntries/enableRefunds/_settleWinningTicket
_transferQuote recipients are sponsorRecipient/protocolTreasury (fixed) or the authenticated owner

findings.title: Adversarial prize semantics can defeat economic delivery while NFT-outcome proceeds are payable
findings.severity: High under the explicit untrusted-prize DESIGN scope; trust limitation under the narrower honest-prize interface scope
required_capabilities: Sponsor selects or controls a prize contract that can fabricate ERC165/ownership responses or later reject/seize/pause outgoing transfers.
Victims buy entries sufficient to meet reserve; normal trusted quote token and timely authenticated VRF callback; no quote-token, wrapper or victim-wallet compromise required.
sequence: Create with a contract that passes the exact configured receipt and reported-ownership checks.
Sell entries, resolve NftWon and permissionlessly settle the valid winning range.
Fabrication variant: token reports winner ownership without honoring the intended ownership/transfer semantics; prize redemption and sponsor release can both appear successful.
Refusal variant: release sponsor proceeds in an earlier transaction, then every NFT redemption reverts. That local rollback cannot recover already paid proceeds; NftWon has no refund transition.
findings.impact: Sponsor can retain 95% of gross sales while an entrant has no enforceable promised NFT delivery. Quote liabilities can remain perfectly conserved: this is a cross-asset economic guarantee/trust gap, not demonstrated quote-ledger insolvency. No other raffle is drained.
exclusions: Not an exploit against an honest, continuously transferable ERC721 with truthful ownership semantics.
The sealed mock uses a separate actualOwner ledger to illustrate dishonest reports; it is not proof of a particular deployed collection or external market value.

Earlier reconciliations source-derived the refusal ordering. The later sealed Gemini ToB a04 S3 paused-prize mock test executed it successfully; reconciliation did not rerun it or validate a deployed collection.

proof.detail: Lines 73-103 define fake semantics; 142-164 demonstrate creation; 167-192 demonstrate buyer payment, fabricated delivery and 95% sponsor payment.
Both tests PASS; adjacent exit code is 0; hashes bound by sealed-artifacts.sha256.
H-1 through H-4 are explicit function fragments of one chain, not four independent High root causes.

proof.kind: newly sealed native executable test source, not reexecuted by reconciliation
proof.detail: MockPrizeNFT pause implementation94–112; actual clone test508–535 pauses after NftWon, settles, releases sponsor proceeds and observes redemption revert with ticket retained. PASS is in separately sealed log. No real deployed prize collection tested.
9 PASS/0FAIL/0SKIP on original solc0.8.36; specifically paused-prize test PASS. Other test names alone are not practical exploit proofs.

remediation_direction: Resolve and consistently state whether adversarial prize semantics are actually supported; no owner acceptance or scope relaxation is inferred.
If restricting assets, validate trusted implementations and their upgrade/pause/seizure authority; ERC165 and self-reported ownerOf cannot establish honesty.

Holding both sponsor and treasury proceeds until delivery plus a bounded refund policy can address refusal, but cannot authenticate a lying token; it also changes winner-dependent liveness and requires a complete policy review.
re_audit_property: Under the chosen supported prize model, entrants cannot lose the retained gross pot without enforceable prize delivery or the specified bounded refund alternative.
Test fabricated receipt/ownerOf, post-escrow pause/seizure, permanent transfer revert, winner refusal, sponsor-before-winner ordering and rollback across separate transactions.
A fix must not claim generic economic authenticity from ownerOf alone.

G3: Buyers of that raffle are not the sponsor, but they opted into an unvetted prize contract; the harm equals entering a raffle for a worthless prize.
G4: BLOCKS

native_fields.unverified: This may add no risk beyond "the prize is worthless". A hostile contract at its own address is simply a worthless collection that buyers can inspect. No on-chain check that only asks the prize contract can fix this.
native_fields.description: The escrow checks cannot enforce DESIGN.md's "untrusted prize" stance; they hold only for honest ERC-721s, which is what IRaffle.sol:14-15 assumes. The recommendation is to document the prize trust boundary for buyers, not to change code.

native_fields.smell: In the NftWon branch, the full sale price for the NFT, sponsorAmount = grossPot - protocolFee (95%), is credited to sponsorProceeds at settlement (Raffle.sol:544, :554). releaseSponsorProceeds (:375-380) pays it with no check of prizeClaimed or winnerRedeemed, so the USDC leg is never tied to the NFT leg (redeemWinningTicket :334-336). No state turns an undeliverable prize into a cash or refund claim: releaseSponsorPrize is barred in NftWon (:397-398), enableRefunds is barred after resolution (:292-293), and there is no deadline or fallback.
native_fields.unverified: Whether a prize that can refuse transferFrom(raffle, winner, id) after escrow is in the threat model. DESIGN.md says "arbitrary prize contracts ... are untrusted", but it also says "Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement", and IRaffle.sol:14-15 says "Supported prizes are honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s". Against a fully malicious prize, coupling alone would not protect buyers either, because the contract could fake delivery. The defect bites hardest for collections that are honest but can restrict transfers (pause, creator transfer-approval hooks, transfer-validator level changes, migrations) and for owner-upgradeable prize contracts.
native_fields.description: Concrete path. (1) Sponsor creates a raffle (reserveEntries = 1,000) whose prize is an owner-upgradeable ERC-721 that passes F:154-179 and the escrow checks at F:128-134. (2) Buyers buy 5,000 entries, so USDC held is 5,000e6. (3) VRF resolves to NftWon. (4) Sponsor upgrades the prize so transfers out of the raffle revert. (5) Anyone calls settleWinningTicket(w): sponsorProceeds = 4,750e6 and protocolFees = 250e6. (6) releaseSponsorProceeds sends 4,750 USDC to sponsorRecipient. (7) redeemWinningTicket(w) reverts at :334 forever. USDC is conserved (5,000 in = 4,750 + 250 out), but the winning-ticket holder is left holding the loss: no NFT and no USDC claim. With an upgradeable prize the sponsor can also recover the NFT. Minimal mitigation if in scope: in releaseSponsorProceeds, require prizeClaimed when status == NftWon. Trade-off: a winner who never redeems then also defers the sponsor's proceeds.

native_fields.smell: In the NftWon branch, Raffle.sol:544 (`sponsorAmount = grossPot - protocolFee`) and :554-555 make 95% of the pot payable to sponsorRecipient and 5% to the treasury. Neither depends on the NFT being delivered. `releaseSponsorProceeds` (:375-382) has no `prizeClaimed`/delivery gate. The only way the NFT leaves is `redeemWinningTicket` (:334-337). It reverts entirely if the prize contract refuses `transferFrom(raffle, ...)` or misreports `ownerOf`. No state converts an undeliverable NftWon prize into cash or refunds: NftWon can never reach Refunding, and `releaseSponsorPrize` is barred in NftWon (:397). The escrow proof at creation also comes from the same untrusted contract: the prize contract can call `onERC721Received` (:421-428) directly, and the factory trusts its `ownerOf` (F:128-132). Trail: (1) a sponsor that administers an upgradeable ERC-721 collection raffles token #1 with reserve 1,000; (2) buyers purchase 5,000 entries (5,000 USDC); (3) VRF resolves NftWon and anyone settles, giving sponsorProceeds = 4,750 USDC (4,750,000,000 raw) and protocolFees = 250 USDC; (4) the sponsor calls releaseSponsorProceeds and receives 4,750 USDC; (5) the sponsor upgrades the collection so any transfer whose `from` is the raffle reverts; (6) every `redeemWinningTicket` by the winning-ticket owner now reverts forever.
native_fields.unverified: Whether sponsor-controlled or admin-mutable prize contracts are in the threat model. DESIGN.md says "arbitrary prize contracts ... are untrusted", but IRaffle.sol:14-15 says "Supported prizes are honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s". DESIGN.md also says "Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement", so the independence is deliberate. Any delivery gate must still handle a winner who never redeems, because there is no redemption deadline. A fully malicious prize can fake both escrow and delivery, so no on-chain change protects against it. The gap is concrete only for admin-mutable collections (upgradeable, pausable or blocklisting).
native_fields.description: The NftWon branch pays the sponsor and treasury for a prize whose delivery depends only on the untrusted prize contract, so a prize that becomes non-transferable after settlement leaves the winning-ticket owner, and the buyers who funded the pot, holding the entire loss.

native_fields.smell: NftWon is a terminal state with no exit if the prize leg can never complete. In NftWon the NFT can only leave through prizeToken.transferFrom(address(this), winner, id) plus the ownerOf re-check (Raffle.sol:334-337). releaseSponsorPrize rejects NftWon (Raffle.sol:397-399). enableRefunds rejects every terminal status (Raffle.sol:279-293). No path turns an undeliverable prize into refunds or cash. Settlement, however, has already credited sponsorProceeds = grossPot - protocolFee (Raffle.sol:544, 554), and releaseSponsorProceeds pays it without checking prizeClaimed (Raffle.sol:375-382). Path: (1) sponsor S escrows token #1 of collection P via createRaffle with reserveEntries = 1,000; (2) buyers buy 1,000 entries = 1,000 USDC; (3) the VRF callback resolves NftWon (Raffle.sol:521); (4) anyone settles: sponsorProceeds = 950 USDC, protocolFees = 50 USDC; (5) anyone calls releaseSponsorProceeds and 950 USDC goes to sponsorRecipient; (6) P permanently blocks transfers out of the clone (admin pause, per-address blocklist, a transfer-validator policy that turns off owner-initiated transfers by contracts, or a sponsor-controlled P whose transferFrom reverts or whose ownerOf lies); (7) every redeemWinningTicket call reverts, which undoes the burn (Raffle.sol:325, 334-337). The winning ticket cannot be refunded either (Raffle.sol:350). Outcome: all 1,000 USDC from buyers is paid out (950 to the sponsor, 50 to the treasury). The winning-ticket holder keeps a claim that can never be redeemed, and the NFT is stuck in the clone with no recovery path.
native_fields.unverified: (a) Whether the trust model makes this reportable. DESIGN.md says arbitrary prize contracts are untrusted, but it also says "Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement", and IRaffle.sol:14-15 limits support to "honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s". (b) Whether blocking delivery adds any loss. If the sponsor controls P, blocking adds nothing over raffling a worthless token: the sponsor collects 950 either way. A sponsor also gains nothing by blocking a valuable token, because it is stuck for them too. Extra loss only appears when a third-party admin of a real collection permanently restricts transfers out of the clone. Working offline, I could not confirm any live collection that accepts the factory's inbound safeTransferFrom (RaffleFactory.sol:128) but later blocks the raffle's outbound transferFrom. (c) A temporary pause only delays the winner: there is no redemption deadline, so they can redeem after the unpause.
native_fields.description: The NftWon branch ties a final state to a delivery made by an untrusted contract while paying the sponsor's 95% with no condition. The smallest code fix is to make releaseSponsorProceeds (Raffle.sol:375-382) require prizeClaimed when status == NftWon, or to add a fallback for failed delivery. Both conflict with DESIGN.md's "claim independently after settlement", and the first lets a winner who never redeems freeze the sponsor's share.

native_fields.root_cause: Raffle.sol:375-378 `releaseSponsorProceeds()` pays out the NftWon sponsor allocation (95% of the pot). `_settleWinningTicket` makes that allocation claimable at settlement (Raffle.sol:543-544, 554). The only guard is `amount == 0` at :377. No `prizeClaimed` (delivery) check is performed. The same gap exists in `releaseProtocolFees()` at Raffle.sol:385-388 for the 5% fee. NftWon also has no way out to refunds: `enableRefunds` reverts for every status except Active and Drawing (Raffle.sol:292-293), and `releaseSponsorPrize` rejects NftWon (Raffle.sol:397-398). So payment and delivery are decoupled. If the prize contract stops honouring the clone's own `transferFrom(raffle -> winner)` at Raffle.sol:334, or the `ownerOf` re-check at :335 fails, every redemption reverts. Meanwhile the sponsor and the treasury are paid in full.
native_fields.internal_pre: Raffle resolved as NftWon (totalEntries >= reserveEntries when the sale ends; Raffle.sol:521).
native_fields.external_pre: After escrow, the prize ERC-721 refuses or redirects the clone's transfer of the prize. Possible causes: the collection admin pauses transfers, applies a transfer restriction (operator, owner-initiated or account freeze that hits the clone), or upgrades the collection. A third possibility is a sponsor-controlled collection whose admin seizes or locks the token. DESIGN.md: "arbitrary prize contracts ... are untrusted". The pause and transfer-restriction behaviours are general ERC-721 ecosystem facts, not code vendored in this repo.
native_fields.impact: The winning-ticket holder bears the whole loss. That is Alice, or anyone who bought the winning ticket on the secondary market at roughly the NFT's value. The NFT she won can never be delivered, and NftWon is terminal with no refund or cash fallback. Meanwhile 100% of the buyers' 12,000 USDC has already gone out: 11,400 to the sponsor recipient and 600 to the treasury. In the seize variant, where S controls the prize contract, S keeps both the NFT and the 11,400 USDC. This breaks money-map invariants 7 (the prize leaves exactly once, to the winner in NftWon) and 15 (every claimant can eventually collect). Suggested severity: Medium, because it depends on an external pre-condition on the prize contract.
native_fields.mitigation: In releaseSponsorProceeds(), and likewise in releaseProtocolFees(), add `if (status == Status.NftWon && !prizeClaimed) revert PrizeNotDelivered();` so the NftWon allocation is paid only against actual delivery. Optionally pair this with an NftWon delivery deadline that turns an undeliverable prize into refunds, so the gated pot cannot be stranded either.

native_fields.root_cause: Raffle.sol:376. `releaseSponsorProceeds` pays out `sponsorProceeds` with no check on `status` or `prizeClaimed`. In `NftWon`, `_settleWinningTicket` allocates 95% to the sponsor and 5% to the treasury (Raffle.sol:543-544, 554-555) through permissionless, storage-only settlement. Neither step depends on the NFT leg in `redeemWinningTicket` (Raffle.sol:329-337) ever succeeding. `NftWon` also has no fallback for the winner: `enableRefunds` only accepts Active or Drawing (Raffle.sol:279-293), `releaseSponsorPrize` excludes NftWon (Raffle.sol:397), and `winnerProceeds` stays 0. The code assumes the escrowed ERC-721 can still be transferred out of the clone when the winner redeems. Real ERC-721s let an admin revoke that after deposit: OpenZeppelin `ERC721Pausable` (`_update` is `whenNotPaused` and reverts `EnforcedPause()`), Manifold Creator Core's admin-set transfer-approval hook (`setApproveTransfer`), Limit Break ERC721-C transfer validators (creator-set soulbound or OTC-blocking policies, account freezing), and upgradeable ERC-721 proxies. DESIGN.md says "arbitrary prize contracts ... are untrusted", but IRaffle.sol:14-15 assumes "honest" prizes. The code follows the weaker of the two.
native_fields.internal_pre: The reserve is met, so the result is `NftWon`. No other state is needed.
native_fields.external_pre: The prize collection has an owner-controlled transfer gate (pause, approve-transfer hook, validator policy or freeze, or proxy upgrade), and the sponsor controls it or colludes with whoever does. The common case qualifies: an artist raffling a token from their own Manifold or OpenZeppelin collection.
native_fields.impact: The buyer cohort paid 20,000 USDC. S takes 19,000 USDC and the treasury 1,000 USDC, and the NFT is never delivered. Winner W is left holding the loss: the claim on C#7 can never be redeemed and there is no cash or refund substitute. This defeats the protocol's trust-minimising guarantee ("Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation") while fully protecting the sponsor's 95%. S's cost is a token S controls anyway.
native_fields.mitigation: In `releaseSponsorProceeds` (Raffle.sol:375-376), add `if (status == Status.NftWon && !prizeClaimed) revert` so NftWon sponsor proceeds unlock only after `redeemWinningTicket` has delivered and verified the prize. Optionally apply the same gate to `releaseProtocolFees`. This narrows DESIGN.md's "claim independently after settlement" for the NftWon branch only. That is the branch where the sponsor can control the opposite leg, and the gate removes the sponsor's profit from blocking the prize.

required_capabilities: Sponsor deliberately or mistakenly chooses the predictable address of a future clone as immutable sponsorRecipient before it is deployed/registered.

Foreign-factory variant additionally needs another deployment and an authorized sponsor/deployer/owner selecting or approving its clone.
sequence: Create A with sponsorRecipient set to future B; B is code-free and not in the registry.
Create B with token ID 2 and verify B equals the predicted address and is now registered.
Cancel empty A into Refunding and release A token ID 1 through unsafe transferFrom; ownerOf==B passes.

findings.impact: An honest NFT selected by the sponsor is stranded and the literal no-inter-clone movement promise is violated. A now-known B also makes a sponsor quote release revert and preserve its immutable liability. Foreign-factory quote donations/recipient payouts can become unaccounted holdings; cross-factory ticket-as-prize composition is a scope violation but not necessarily permanent loss.
exclusions: No attacker can transform an arbitrary existing victim EOA into a chosen clone.
No theft of another raffle’s quote balance, winner manipulation, or reduction of buyer refund liability is established.

Later sealed Claude S6 executes the future-clone quote-release rejection; later sealed Daybreak S6 executes owner-selected ticket delivery to an existing other-factory clone. Counterfactual address predictability alone does not authorize an attacker to select another user’s recipient. CREATE2 or prevrandao address changes are not complete destination-safety or claim-recovery remedies.

native_fields.smell: All four USDC exits re-screen the payee at payout time via _transferQuote -> _isProtocolDestination (Raffle.sol:565). The NFT exit releaseSponsorPrize (:402-405) sends the prize to sponsorRecipient with no payout-time screen. sponsorRecipient is screened only once, at initialize (:193-195), and isRaffle is queried only when the address already has code (:602-603). F:166 likewise checks only raffles that are already registered.
native_fields.unverified: Any victim other than the sponsor. The screen result can flip only if sponsorRecipient is a code-less address that later becomes a factory clone (the CREATE address keccak(rlp(factory, nonce)), via OZ Clones.clone). Minimal mitigation: in releaseSponsorPrize, revert if _isProtocolDestination(recipient, address(prizeToken)), mirroring _transferQuote.

native_fields.smell: `_isProtocolDestination` only queries `isRaffle` when `destination.code.length != 0` (Raffle.sol:602-604). Clones are deployed with CREATE from the factory (OZ Clones.clone), so their addresses are predictable from the factory nonce. A sponsorRecipient set to a not-yet-deployed clone address therefore passes F:_validateCreateParams (F:163-169) and initialize (Raffle.sol:193-195). The same applies to a ticket sent to such an address. Once that clone exists, releaseSponsorProceeds reverts with InvalidQuoteDestination forever (Raffle.sol:565). releaseSponsorPrize has no runtime screen at all, so it moves the prize into the other clone via transferFrom (Raffle.sol:402-405). This contradicts DESIGN.md: "Never move assets between raffle clones".

native_fields.smell: DESIGN.md requires "Never move assets between raffle clones." `sponsorRecipient` is screened only at creation: `RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams` checks the `isRaffle` mapping (RaffleFactory.sol:163-169), and `Raffle.initialize` calls `_isProtocolDestination` (Raffle.sol:193), which skips the `isRaffle` query for addresses with no code (:602). Clones are deployed with CREATE (OZ `Clones.clone`: `create(value, 0x09, 0x37)`), so each future raffle address depends only on the factory address and nonce. These addresses can be predicted, and anyone can advance the nonce through the permissionless `createRaffle`. A sponsorRecipient equal to a future clone address therefore passes both screens. After a later `createRaffle` registers a raffle at that address, `releaseSponsorPrize` (:402-405) transfers the prize NFT into that clone without a delivery-time screen, and no function can ever move it out. The USDC path for the same recipient, `_transferQuote`, re-screens at payout (:565) and reverts, which strands `sponsorProceeds` instead. The same skip for code-less addresses in `_update` (:498 → :602) lets a ticket be sent to a future clone address, where it later becomes unreachable.
native_fields.unverified: No actor other than the sponsor (for sponsorRecipient) or the ticket owner or operator (for tickets) chooses these destinations. Pointing at the raffle's own address is caught (:599, `destination == address(this)`), and a recipient that is already a raffle is caught (RaffleFactory.sol:166; Raffle.sol:602-603). On current evidence this harms only the party who chose the address, so it is not reportable as a finding. It is listed because it is the one reachable state that violates DESIGN.md's cross-clone invariant, and because sibling payout sites screen inconsistently.
native_fields.description: Re-running `_isProtocolDestination(recipient, address(prizeToken))` before Raffle.sol:404 would make the NFT payout behave like `_transferQuote`, but because sponsorRecipient is immutable the prize would still be stranded rather than moved.

native_fields.smell: USDC payouts re-screen the recipient at payout time through _transferQuote (Raffle.sol:564-567). The two NFT payouts, releaseSponsorPrize (Raffle.sol:404) and redeemWinningTicket NftWon (Raffle.sol:334), do not. Two earlier screens both accept a not-yet-deployed CREATE address of the factory's next clone as sponsorRecipient: the init-time screen (Raffle.sol:193 via _isProtocolDestination, which skips the registry for code-less addresses at :602) and the factory screen (F:166, isRaffle mapping). Once a clone is created at that address, anyone can call releaseSponsorPrize and push the prize into another raffle clone. That breaks DESIGN.md "Never move assets between raffle clones", and the NFT cannot be recovered there (no rescue path, Raffle.sol:410-411). releaseSponsorProceeds meanwhile reverts with InvalidQuoteDestination forever.
native_fields.unverified: No third-party victim: only the sponsor chooses sponsorRecipient, so the loss is self-inflicted, and the receiving clone's own accounting is unaffected. The ticket-side sibling (_update, Raffle.sol:498, same code-less gap) is also self-harm only.
native_fields.description: The destination screen is applied unevenly across asset types and can be bypassed with counterfactual clone addresses, so the spec invariant is enforced for USDC but not for the prize NFT.

native_fields.smell: `releaseSponsorProceeds` (Raffle.sol:375-382), `releaseProtocolFees` (:385-392) and `releaseSponsorPrize` (:402-405) can only pay the recipients fixed at initialize (:198-199); the treasury is also a factory immutable. Ticket-backed claims (`refundTickets`, `redeemWinningTicket`) have an escape: the holder can transfer the bearer ticket to a clean address. The sponsor and treasury claims have no such path. If USDC blacklists `sponsorRecipient` after settlement, or blacklists the factory-wide `protocolTreasury` at any time, `_transferQuote` -> `safeTransfer` (:564-567) reverts permanently. The allocated USDC is then locked in the clone forever, and for the treasury this hits every raffle from the factory.
native_fields.unverified: Whether recipient-level USDC blacklisting is in scope for a "trusted canonical dependency". The loss falls only on the sponsor or the protocol, never on buyers, so this is likely Low/Info.
native_fields.description: Sibling asymmetry: ticket claims can be re-routed by transferring the bearer ticket, but sponsor and treasury claims are pinned to immutable recipients with no fallback, so a USDC freeze on a recipient strands those funds permanently.

findings.title: Receiver acceptance and address-level ownership do not prove bearer claim usability
required_capabilities: Payer/owner/approved operator selects a receiver that accepts the ticket or NFT but cannot later issue the required claim/transfer call; includes inaccessible future or foreign addresses.
sequence: Safe mint/transfer succeeds or unsafe prize delivery establishes address-level ownership.
Recipient has no usable calling route to exercise the bearer right.
findings.impact: Owner-selected claim can be inaccessible despite intact accounting. General last-actor-exit claims require a capable recipient assumption.
exclusions: No involuntary loss of a normal EOA established.
A receiver hook acceptance is not a promise of arbitrary future call functionality; runtime sink checks cannot classify every arbitrary contract.
remediation_direction: Document capability requirements; enforce known sink checks; if alternate payout is desired, authenticate current bearer ownership and avoid arbitrary caller routing.
re_audit_property: Current owner, former owner, operator and incapable receivers must be distinguished; accounting solvency must not be equated with universal claim usability.

model_disagreements.resolution: Unsafe prize return is a recipient capability issue with separately reproduced sponsor-selected future-clone subset; own-recipient loss, not general theft.
Counterfactual destination can strand its own chosen custody; permissionless settlement isolates unrelated claims. Native demotion to lead preserved beside Low/Info assessments.

findings.title: Unsolicited assets have no rescue and are outside recorded liabilities
required_capabilities: A sender donates quote tokens, forces native currency, or unsafely transfers an unrelated NFT to the raffle.
sequence: Asset custody increases without a protocol purchase, allocation or configured prize transition.
No general rescue/execution method exists; only configured claims/prize can exit.
findings.impact: Donated assets can be irretrievable. They do not create a liability to the donor, authorize a drain, or make existing claims insolvent under trusted token semantics.
exclusions: Do not count raw custody as owed liability. A donation can make actual quote balance exceed accounted liabilities; equality is valid only in a no-donation model.
Counterfactual sponsor-prize delivery in RF-002 is a protocol-directed transfer and is not dismissed as an unsolicited donation.
remediation_direction: Explicitly document no-rescue behavior and scope accounting invariants. A rescue authority would change the immutability/authority model and must not sweep recorded claims.
re_audit_property: Assert balance >= liabilities under donation scenarios; prove all legitimate claims remain payable and unrelated donations cannot modify settlement or ownership rights.

sequence: Modulo maps outputs to 1..totalEntries with at most one-preimage frequency difference.

exclusions: Not an exact-uniformity proof; not counted as a security finding.
remediation_direction: Retain explicit randomness assumptions; no complex redesign recommended solely for this negligible bound.
re_audit_property: Selection must remain in sold range and authenticated; quantify bias rather than claim perfect uniformity.

findings.title: Sponsor buying reserve-crossing entries changes the openly specified outcome
required_capabilities: Sponsor pays the same price as other entrants before sale end.
sequence: Buy enough entries to meet the publicly defined reserve, increasing NFT-outcome likelihood and sponsor proceeds.
findings.impact: Strategic participation is permitted by the open sale; no protected cash-outcome entitlement or unauthorized free entries established.
exclusions: No sybil-resistant restriction implied by source; independent NFT valuation not audited.
remediation_direction: Disclose reserve mechanics; a sponsor participation restriction would be a new economic policy requiring sybil analysis.
re_audit_property: Every counted sponsor entry must transfer the same canonical quote amount and receive the same range semantics.
model_disagreements: Gemini FP-L-01 labels the documented reserve cliff/sponsor top-up/single-buyer cash outcome Low. Reconciliation closes it as configured economics; address-only sponsor-buy bans are sybil-bypassable and no minimum-two-buyer rule exists.

model_disagreements.resolution: Reserve crossing and sponsor self-purchase are the disclosed payout rule. The example depends on NFT valuation, capital and winning odds; no unauthorized withdrawal or guaranteed-profit defect established.

Uncapped pre-deadline paid entries dilute every prior entry under the published odds rule. Sponsor rebate is the configured seller economics; no fixed odds promise shown. Preserve Medium dissent, not promote design choice to proven theft.
Single-owner CashWon applies the explicit80/15/5split; ticketCount is not distinct participant count.
Sponsor paid purchases, reserve crossing and dilution follow disclosed economics. Native finding/confidence retained; no fixed odds/no-sponsor promise established.
95% payout above reserve is the configured seller share; requires a product-policy change to cap. No unauthorized fund extraction proved.
Caller pays a disclosed native VRF fee; CashWon is an explicit outcome. Sponsor cannot veto other permissionless callers; withholding alone is not control of the draw.

G1: ALLOWS

buyEntries (:215-221) checks only status, sale time, recipient, count and overflow; it has no cap once the reserve is met and no exclusion of sponsor-controlled buyers. _update (:497-502) screens only protocol plumbing.
G2: ALLOWS

Sponsor capital is locked only from endTime-1 until settle plus release (minutes to hours), and 95% comes back in NftWon. It is not flash-loanable, but the attack pays whenever NFT value > 5% of the final pot; sybil purchases cannot be told apart from real ones.
G3: Victims are the organic ticket holders who bought before the sale closed: their odds of winning the NFT are diluted while their USDC goes to sponsorRecipient and the treasury.
G4: ALLOWS
Expected value moves between cohorts. R07 example: Alice -9,000 USDC EV, sponsor +4,500, treasury +4,500.

native_fields.root_cause: Raffle.sol:544 (`sponsorAmount = grossPot - protocolFee`, with grossPot = unsettledPot at :539, credited at :554) pays the sponsor 95% of the whole pot, including entries the sponsor bought through any address. `buyEntries` (Raffle.sol:215-233) has no entry cap once `reserveEntries` is met and does not exclude the rebated party. Each sponsor-funded entry therefore costs the sponsor only 5% of ENTRY_PRICE but carries full weight in the uniform draw (Raffle.sol:518). This breaks DESIGN.md's uniform "one entry costs 1,000,000 units" for exactly one cohort. Earlier buyers cannot exit after the sponsor's late purchase: refunds open only at endTime+2d (Raffle.sol:286-287), and anyone, including the sponsor, can draw at endTime (Raffle.sol:242).
native_fields.internal_pre: The raffle resolves NftWon (totalEntries >= reserveEntries, Raffle.sol:521). The sponsor controls or colludes with sponsorRecipient, which is the default setup. The attack pays off whenever the NFT value V > 0.05 * organic entries N.
native_fields.external_pre: The sponsor has k USDC available from the last block before endTime until releaseSponsorProceeds, typically minutes: requestDraw at endTime, then 30 confirmations, then settle and release. 95% of it comes back. A flash loan does not work because entries lock funds across transactions.
native_fields.impact: The cohort of organic ticket holders who bought before the sale closed is left holding the loss.
native_fields.mitigation: Stop the sale at the reserve in buyEntries (`if (lastEntry > reserveEntries) revert ...`), so no sponsor-rebated entries can be minted after organic demand meets the reserve. A buyer blocklist on sponsor/sponsorRecipient alone is not enough, because purchases are permissionless (sybil). A sponsor fill of the gap below the reserve remains possible; it is tracked as a separate lead.

native_fields.smell: (Outside the DoS lens; passed on to the economic/cross-cohort lens.) Only totalEntries >= reserveEntries decides the outcome (Raffle.sol:521), and nothing excludes entries the sponsor paid for. NftWon pays grossPot - fee back to the sponsor (Raffle.sol:544). So buying whatever is missing from the reserve costs the sponsor only the 5% fee on those entries, and lets it flip a raffle that missed its reserve after seeing demand. Path: reserve 10,000; organic buyers hold 2,000 entries (2,000 USDC) one block before endTime. The honest outcome would be CashWon: winner 1,600, sponsor 300 + NFT, treasury 100. Instead the sponsor buys 8,000 entries from a fresh address. The callback gives NftWon; settlement pays the sponsor 9,500 (net +1,500 on an 8,000 outlay), and the sponsor's address holds 80% of entries for its own NFT. With an NFT value V = 3,000 USDC, organic buyers' expected value falls from 1,600 to 600 (-1,000), the sponsor's rises from 3,300 to 3,900 (+600), and the treasury's from 100 to 500 (+400). These sum to zero.
native_fields.unverified: This is not a DoS issue. It is unclear whether DESIGN.md means the reserve to protect only the sponsor, in which case a sponsor buying in is the same as having set a lower reserve. Addresses the sponsor controls cannot be identified on-chain, so any fix is at the design level.
native_fields.description: Buyers rely on the 80% cash payout when the reserve is missed, but the sponsor can cancel it at 5% cost by buying in at the last moment, after seeing demand.

Nothing in buyEntries (L209-237) or _update (L497-502) excludes the sponsor or sponsorRecipient as buyer or recipient. The losses are expected-value transfers, not deterministic theft.
native_fields.description: Because L544 rebates 95% of the sponsor's own spend, a last-block dilution or reserve flip has positive expected value for the sponsor. Non-sponsor buyers carry the loss, and the treasury captures part of it.

native_fields.smell: In NftWon, `sponsorAmount = grossPot - protocolFee` (Raffle.sol:544) is computed on the gross pot. That pot includes entries the sponsor bought itself, from any address. So each sponsor-funded entry costs the sponsor 5% net, while every other entrant pays 100%. Because buyEntries (:209-237) stays open until endTime, the sponsor can watch demand and shill-enter in the last block, diluting buyers' odds and keeping its NFT. Numbers: the NFT is worth 10,000 USDC and the reserve is 2,000. Buyers purchase 2,000 entries (2,000 USDC). Just before endTime the sponsor buys 18,000 entries from a fresh address. NftWon with a pot of 20,000 gives sponsorProceeds 19,000 and fee 1,000. The sponsor ends +1,000 USDC net and keeps the NFT with probability 0.9. Buyers' expected value drops from 10,000 to 1,000 USDC (-9,000). The sponsor gains +8,100 and the treasury +900 (checked arithmetically). This is profitable whenever the NFT is worth more than 5% of the final pot. In CashWon a self-entry nets -5% (0.80 winner share + 0.15 sponsor share), so only NftWon is exposed.
native_fields.unverified: Whether sponsor participation is an accepted design risk. The money map says the sponsor "may also buy entries" and DESIGN.md is silent. Excluding addresses is defeated by Sybil addresses, so there is no one-line mitigation. This is an economic/game-theory issue at the edge of the flow-symmetry lens.
native_fields.description: The 95% sponsor share refunds the sponsor's own entries, so a sponsor can shill-enter at a 5% cost to win back its prize with high probability, and honest entrants hold the loss.

native_fields.smell: The NftWon/CashWon regime check (Raffle.sol:521) counts sponsor-bought entries, which are rebated 95% through sponsorProceeds (Raffle.sol:544). When organic demand N < reserve R, the sponsor can fill R-N in the last block before endTime at a 5% cost. That turns a CashWon raffle (buyers' EV 0.8 USDC per entry) into NftWon. Example with R = 1,000, N = 900, NFT worth V = 500 USDC: honest CashWon gives buyers 720 USDC EV and the sponsor 135 USDC + the NFT (635). If the sponsor buys 100 entries, the raffle becomes NftWon: sponsor = 950 - 100 + 0.1*500 = 900 (+265); buyers' EV = 0.9*500 = 450 (-270); treasury +5.
native_fields.unverified: (1) Whether under-reserve buyers are entitled to expect CashWon. The reserve may be meant only as sponsor protection, and organic demand reaching R gives the same regime. (2) The flip pays only when V is below roughly 0.8*R (an overpriced reserve); with V = 900 in the example it is unprofitable and helps buyers. (3) There is no sybil-proof code fix: the sale cap proposed for the dilution FINDING does not close this gap.
native_fields.description: A sponsor-funded fill of the gap below the reserve in the last block lets the sponsor choose the payout regime after seeing demand, at a 5% cost, and moves EV from under-reserve buyers to the sponsor.

native_fields.smell: The VRF wrapper can never change. RaffleFactory stores it as an immutable (RaffleFactory.sol:86), builds it into the single implementation (RaffleFactory.sol:89, inherited immutable i_vrfV2PlusWrapper), has no admin to repoint it, and createRaffle (RaffleFactory.sol:97-148) never checks that the wrapper still works. If the wrapper is disabled or unconfigured, getVrfRequestPrice and requestRandomnessPayInNative (Raffle.sol:249, 257) revert for every raffle. If the wrapper's subscription runs out of funds, a paid request is accepted but never fulfilled. After such an event, sponsors can still create raffles and buyers can still buy (Raffle.sol:209-237), but no raffle can ever resolve. Each one only moves to Refunding at endTime + 2d (Raffle.sol:286-287) or drawRequestedAt + 2d (Raffle.sol:290-291). Buyers' USDC and sponsors' NFTs are locked for up to 30d of sale + 2d (or + 4d). In the unfunded case, whoever requests the draw loses the native VRF fee.
native_fields.unverified: The wrapper implementation is not in node_modules; only VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.sol and IVRFV2PlusWrapper.sol are. The disabled and unfunded behaviour therefore comes from public Chainlink v2.5 semantics, not from source in the repo. No principal is lost because the refund path stays intact. DESIGN.md treats the wrapper as a trusted canonical dependency and rules out mutable configuration, so this is probably accepted design. The impact is limited to time-bounded locking.
native_fields.description: Because the wrapper is immutable and never checked, a deprecation on Chainlink's side puts every live and future raffle into a "lock, then refund" mode that only redeploying the factory can fix.

native_fields.smell: _update (Raffle.sol:497-502) only screens destinations, so tickets can still move during Drawing: after requestDraw (:252) and before fulfillRandomWords (:509-524) records the result. winningEntry = randomWords[0] % totalEntries + 1 (:518) follows deterministically from the VRF proof in the pending Chainlink fulfillment transaction. A mempool observer can therefore know the winning ticket before the callback is included and act ahead of it: (a) fill standing collection-wide offers with tickets known to lose, or (b) buy the winning ticket from a pending listing. Chainlink's VRF guidance is to stop accepting inputs once randomness has been requested.
native_fields.unverified: The VRF v2.5 coordinator is not vendored in node_modules, so I did not verify how the word is derived from the proof or whether fulfillments pass through the public mempool. native_fields.description: Tickets stay transferable while the draw outcome can be worked out publicly from the pending VRF fulfillment, so informed holders can offload losing tickets or snipe the winning ticket from counterparties who don't know the result.

native_fields.smell: _update (Raffle.sol:497-502) allows ticket transfers in every status, including Drawing (the NatSpec at Raffle.sol:491 says so deliberately). The pending VRF fulfillment (wrapper -> rawFulfillRandomWords -> Raffle.sol:518) lets any mempool observer work out winningEntry before it executes. The observer can fill a stale marketplace listing of the winning ticket, or sell a losing ticket into a standing collection bid, ahead of or bundled right after the callback. Example: Alice lists ticket #7 (500 of 1,000 entries; NFT worth 2,000 USDC) at 900 USDC. Bob simulates the pending fulfillment, sees that entry 742 (in #7) wins, fills the listing first, and redeems the NFT. Alice's EV falls from about 1,000 to about 450.
native_fields.unverified: (1) Whether Chainlink's mainnet VRF fulfillments go through the public mempool. (2) Whether any fillable marketplace order exists at fulfillment time. (3) A Drawing-only transfer lock can be bypassed by bundling [fulfillment, fill], because status becomes NftWon mid-bundle. The only robust fix, blocking operator-initiated transfers from requestDraw onward, conflicts with the documented bearer-claim design. Victims are external order makers; the protocol's own accounting is unaffected.
native_fields.description: Tickets stay tradeable while the draw result can be derived publicly but is not yet on-chain, which allows trades against stale secondary-market orders by someone who already knows the result.

native_fields.smell: Tickets stay transferable in Drawing. `_update` (Raffle.sol:497-502) screens only the destination, never the status. The VRF callback (Raffle.sol:518-521) is the only state change between "random word exists" and "winner recorded". Anyone who can read a pending fulfillment can compute winningEntry = word % totalEntries + 1 before it lands. They can then buy the winning ticket from an open listing, taking the prize from the seller, or sell losing tickets into open collection offers, passing the loss to the bidder. This is the Phase-4 pattern of joining just before a distribution or leaving just before a loss.
native_fields.unverified: Two things are unverified. First, whether VRF v2.5 fulfillment transactions on the target chain are visible in a public mempool before inclusion; the wrapper/coordinator source is not vendored under packages/contracts. Second, whether ticket listings or offers exist on any marketplace during Drawing.
native_fields.description: If fulfillment calldata is public before inclusion, a searcher can bundle a fill of the listed winning ticket ahead of the callback and take the NFT or the 80% cash from the seller. Blocking ticket transfers while status == Drawing would close the window.

native_fields.smell: (Outside the DoS lens; passed on.) Tickets stay transferable while status == Drawing. Raffle.sol:497-502 only screens destinations, and Raffle.sol:491 says tickets are transferable "in every lifecycle state". So the input that decides who gets paid, ticket ownership, can change after the VRF request. The calldata of the coordinator's fulfillment fixes randomWords[0]. Anyone watching the mempool can therefore compute winningEntry = randomWords[0] % totalEntries + 1 (Raffle.sol:518) and the ticket that contains it before the callback lands. They can then trade ahead of it: buy the winning ticket from an open listing, or sell known losing tickets into open collection offers. Path: a CashWon raffle with 1,000 entries and a 1,000 USDC pot. Holder H has an open listing for ticket #7 (entries 101-110) at 9 USDC. The fulfillment transaction is pending, and its random word maps to entry 105. A bot fills H's listing at 9 USDC before the callback, then calls redeemWinningTicket(7) after resolution and receives 800 USDC (Raffle.sol:339-342). H gives up about 791 USDC of value.
native_fields.unverified: I could not confirm offline whether Ethereum-mainnet VRF fulfillments go through the public mempool. Even if they do not, a back-run right after resolution sniping a stale listing causes the same loss to the seller. That makes the protocol's share of the blame small and mostly a question of listing hygiene. Chainlink advises against accepting inputs after a randomness request. The smallest change would be for _update to reject ticket transfers that are neither mints nor burns while status == Drawing, but that removes only the pre-resolution window.
native_fields.description: Because tickets remain transferable during Drawing, anyone who reads the pending fulfillment can trade against counterparties who cannot see it.

assurance_issues.title: Swallowed reverts permit an entirely inactive invariant campaign
assurance_issues.confidence: high for demonstrated experiment; bounded reachability limits retained
assurance_issues.detail: All 9 invariants survived a valid-purchase-always-reverts mutant at 64 runs/depth64; audit_strict 16/depth64 also passed with zero handler reverts. Unit/fuzz/security selection killed it with59 failures. RaffleHandler.sol:61-72 catches purchase failures; many actions silently return; no minimum meaningful activity is proved.
assurance_issues.capabilities: Test harness controls generated actions, callers, time and caught exceptions; no deployed attacker claim.
assurance_issues.remedy: Track independent attempted/successful/unexpected-failure counters; assert allowed actions succeed; seed terminal branches without requiring every random sequence to hit all branches.
assurance_issues.re_audit_property: A contract that rejects all valid purchases must fail a stateful campaign; successful cash/NFT/refund settlement and final exits must have measured witnesses.

assurance_issues.confidence: high for demonstrated experiment; bounded reachability limits retained
assurance_issues.detail: The stateful handler pranks owner for redemption/refunds (RaffleHandler.sol:187-188,207-208), so removing winner owner guard survived all9 bounded invariants. Existing deterministic/fuzz/security tests killed it with3 failures. Two holder addresses do not provide adversarial caller coverage.

assurance_issues.re_audit_property: Unauthorized claim attempts must fail with complete state rollback; current bearer must still succeed.

native_custom_check_ledger.native_title: Raffle state-changing entry points with external interactions are nonReentrant (except documented allowlist)
All quote-token safeTransfer calls are inside _transferQuote
Per-raffle configuration variables are written only by initialize()
status is written only by constructor/initialize/onERC721Received/requestDraw/enableRefunds/fulfillRandomWords
fulfillRandomWords: no explicit revert/require/assert, no external interaction, no loop
_settleWinningTicket performs no external interaction (storage-only settlement)
Prize transfers only in redeem/releaseSponsorPrize, each reads+writes prizeClaimed and verifies ownerOf
Raffle._update screens destinations via _isProtocolDestination and delegates to ERC721._update
No delegatecall/selfdestruct/ecrecover/blockhash/tx.origin/prevrandao in production contracts
createRaffle: clone -> initialize -> register(isRaffle) -> untrusted prize safeTransferFrom
unsettledPot written only by buyEntries/enableRefunds/_settleWinningTicket
_transferQuote recipients are sponsorRecipient/protocolTreasury (fixed) or the authenticated owner

limits: S6-F1 one-block-early VRF/marketplace exploit assertion is not established by the mock test; the operator chooses word7 and manually pranks the transferor. Keep LEAD-001 unproved external-ordering preconditions.

The45-property ledger is not45 universal proofs. SM-3/SM-12/EI-2 require truthful prize behavior; ownerOf checking cannot prove actual delivery for malicious tokens. T-3 only screens current protocol code and can become false at a later future-clone address.
EI-1 wording every value-moving entry point nonReentrant is broader than custom C1, whose explicit allowlist includes inherited ticket transfers/callbacks. Do not discard that allowlist.
ST-1 passing Slither interface checks is not complete ERC721 standards conformance. Missing repository tests/scripts in an intentionally source-only context is not proof the repository lacks them.

Native TP-accepted Slither statuses and action-plan acceptance are reviewer triage, never current owner acceptance. No sponsor-capping redesign or payout gate is an approved fix; complete both-bucket liability/fallback analysis is required.

Before final campaign, the native harness corrected settle-on-redeem cash winnerProceeds expectation and a nonpayable assertion constructor. These retained failures are test artifacts, not production defects.

Echidna/Medusa use two raffles/four actors; ordinary entry counts1..25 plus buyHuge, refund batches<=8 with corruption modes, bounded warps. Full100-ticket batches, dishonest prize-delivery verification branches and wrapper paidPrice>msg.value were not universally exercised. No Manticore execution; disclosed Halmos substitution.

echidna.scope: single-actor purchase-only; at most64 successful buys per state
